item.description: Nov 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Florida State Seminoles quarterback Ashton Daniels (14) reacts as time expires and the Seminoles defeat the Pittsburgh Panthers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Florida State football enters Friday’s rivalry showdown against No. 20 Florida with its postseason hopes hanging in the balance. However, the Seminoles face another significant question as they prepare to host the Gators at Doak Campbell Stadium. Interim coach Rick Stockstill has addressed the possibility of making a quarterback change if Florida State’s offense continues to struggle. Florida State Quarterback Situation Draws Attention Ashton Daniels remains Florida State’s starting quarterback entering Friday’s matchup. However, Stockstill acknowledged earlier this week that a change could become necessary depending on performance. The comments followed Daniels’ difficult outing against North Carolina State. Daniels completed 19 of 36 passes for 206 yards and two interceptions in the Seminoles’ 28-10 loss. The senior has thrown 14 touchdowns and 14 interceptions this season. Additionally, his 14 interceptions lead the Football Bowl Subdivision. Nevertheless, Stockstill defended his quarterback while acknowledging that the offense must improve. The interim coach emphasized that he would not make a change simply for the sake of making one. Instead, any adjustment would depend on whether another quarterback could give the Seminoles a better opportunity to win. Florida State Faces Must-Win Situation The stakes could hardly be higher for Florida State. The Seminoles enter Friday at 5-6 and must defeat Florida to qualify for a bowl game. Another loss would leave the program with a third consecutive losing season. Meanwhile, Florida has already secured postseason eligibility under first-year coach Jon Sumrall. The Gators improved to 7-4 after defeating Vanderbilt last Saturday. Florida has also won its last two meetings against Florida State. Consequently, the Seminoles must find a way to reverse their recent struggles against their biggest in-state rival. Florida Defense Presents Difficult Challenge Florida State’s quarterback situation becomes even more important when considering the Gators’ defensive personnel. Florida edge rusher Jayden Woods enters the matchup with seven sacks. Meanwhile, Emmanuel Oyebadejo has contributed five sacks. Both defenders could create problems for a Florida State offense that has struggled with consistency. However, Daniels remains dangerous as a runner. The former Auburn quarterback has scored 13 rushing touchdowns this season, setting Florida State’s single-season record for a quarterback. His mobility could give the Seminoles opportunities to extend drives and challenge Florida’s defense. Nevertheless, turnovers remain a significant concern. item.description: USA TODAY Sports St. John Bosco football coach Jason Negro isn’t shy about where he believes the CIF Southern Section stands in the national high school football conversation. And he has the résumé to make the argument. “Without question, the CIF Southern Section Division 1 (playoffs) is, in my opinion, the best in the entire country, and I can say that because we’ve played all across the country,” Negro said in an interview with SoCal Prep Report . “A lot of the teams in the division were able to [play out-of-state teams] as well and be quite successful in doing that year in and year out.” Negro then offered a challenge to anyone who disagrees. “If anybody wants to challenge that, they can always come to California and play us in our state or we’ll go and travel and play you in yours.” St. John Bosco's Jason Negro says on @SoCalPrepReport the CIF Southern Section D1 playoffs are the best in the country. "If anyone wants to challenge that, they can always come to CA and play us … or we'll travel and play you in yours." The numbers and recent results give the longtime St. John Bosco coach plenty of ammunition. The Southern Section has produced some of the country’s top high school football programs, led by the likes of St. John Bosco and Mater Dei. Those teams haven’t just built their reputations by beating each other in the Trinity League, they’ve taken their brands on the road and collected wins against nationally recognized opponents. St. John Bosco Has Made a Habit of Winning on the Road St. John Bosco has been one of the most aggressive programs in the country when it comes to scheduling national competition. The Braves followed that with another road win against Central Catholic of Portland, Oregon, before returning to California to navigate the Trinity League and Southern Section playoffs. That season ended with St. John Bosco beating Mater Dei 24-22 in the CIF Southern Section Division 1 championship game and defeating Serra of San Mateo for the CIF State Open Division title. The Braves finished as national champions, according to multiple national ranking outlets. The following season brought another major road test. item.description: Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The Miami Marlins finally broke their offseason silence by bringing veteran catcher Gary Sanchez aboard, according to Yahoo Sports . This one-year deal could reach $6.5 million, marking the largest contract for a position player in president of baseball operations Peter Bendix tenure. According to an individual familiar with the discussions, The Associated Press was informed that the deal was finalized on Wednesday night. Since the regular season concluded, this marks the initial known free agent signing executed by the franchise. Although this transaction addresses a particular weakness, the front office must go further to build upon an 80-win campaign. Fixing the Left-Handed Gap Sanchez offers a right-handed bat that Miami desperately needs against southpaws. Last year, the squad performed poorly versus left-handed pitching, finishing 27th in wRC+ and achieving an 85 wRC+ in that metric. His batting average sat at .209 for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, yet he achieved a far superior .801 OPS against left-handed pitching. This specific skill set targets a key vulnerability in the lineup. Sanchez turns 34 next week and will likely serve as a backup to starting catcher Joe Mack. His role may shift to designated hitter or late-game pinch-hitter duties to maximize his offensive value while limiting his defensive exposure. The Rotation Needs a Lefty Ace Securing Sanchez resolves one issue, yet the rotation remains vulnerable and ready for a significant upgrade. Sandy Alcantara stays the ace, while Eury Perez demonstrated moments of brilliance despite a volatile season. Following a neck injury that ended his season early, Max Meyer is anticipated to be prepared for spring training. Beyond those three, the depth is thin. Tyler Phillips battled home runs after entering the rotation, whereas Janson Junk and Ryan Gusto demonstrated adequacy. A left-handed starter capable of consuming innings and preventing runners from reaching base is required by the team. To complement their young core, the Marlins ought to pursue Shota Imanaga. Across his three stateside seasons, his ERAs were 2.91, 3.73, and 3.77. Despite worries regarding his propensity to surrender home runs, Fish On First noted Imanaga has been a reliable starter. item.title: Atley Calvert recalled, looks to make NHL debut tonight
item.description: COLUMBUS, OH - SEPTEMBER 24: Pittsburgh Penguins forward Atley Calvert (84) controls the puck as Columbus Blue Jackets forward Adam Fantilli (19) gives chase during a preseason NHL game between the Columbus Blue Jackets and Pittsburgh Penguins on September 24, 2025, at Nationwide Arena in Columbus, OH. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Penguins announced a recall from the minors this morning, forward Atley Calvert joins the NHL roster for the first time. Forward Atley Calvert has been recalled from the @WBSPenguins (AHL). pic.twitter.com/TYYH4DzjaD — Pittsburgh Penguins (@penguins) November 27, 2026 It’s a great story for the 23-year old slowly but surely climbing the ranks. The undrafted Calvert started out with an AHL contract with the Pens back in 2024. He split time between the ECHL and AHL in his first pro season. Last year, he became a key player in Wilkes-Barre, scoring 38 points in 70 games and excelling in a variety of roles, including playing some center when the team was short and needed the help. Calvert was rewarded with his first NHL contract last off-season. He’s been one of the top players to Wilkes-Barre this year, producing 15 points in 20 games. “He has, really, a lot of pro qualities to his game that I think can translate,” assistant GM Jason Spezza said back at training camp . “He’s a winger that can play center. He’s a bit of a Swiss Army knife for us. So, a guy the coaches really lean on down there in different ways. I think at times maybe it’s the short end of the stick offensively because he’s so reliable defensively, and in kind of the roles that coaches like to use guys.” Many players have been recalled, which hasn’t always meant finding time in the game lineup. That doesn’t look to be the case this time around, despite having Justin Brazeau and Andrei Kuzmenko on hand, the Pens put Calvert in a position that suggests he will make his NHL debut tonight in Buffalo. Atley Calvert is taking line rushes 👀 Rakell-Crosby-Malkin Novak-Kindel-Hayes McGroarty-Lapierre-Koivunen Dewar-Lizotte-Calvert (Brazeau, Kuzmenko) Korczak-Karlsson Girard-van Riemsdyk Carlile-Letang (Stastney) — Pens Inside Scoop (@PensInsideScoop) November 27, 2026 Defenseman Declan Carlile rotated back into the playing lineup and the experiment of trying Kaedan Korczak with Erik Karlsson looks like it will restart tonight. All of that pales compared to another tangible step of the youth movement encroaching on the Penguins. Pittsburgh only has a roster spot available as long as Egor Chinakhov remains on IR, so Calvert’s first taste of NHL action could be short-lived. However, it likely won’t be his only opportunity to play NHL games this season since it’s expected the Pens will be shifting gears in the near future and starting to trade away veterans on the roster and open up more places for younger players like Calvert. Another step in that journey looks like it will take place tonight.

item.title: Raiders defense is doing well in this area
item.description: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense, overall, has been having a rough season. However, the unit is doing one thing very well — creating turnovers. Las Vegas has 17 takeaways, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. Many of the Raiders’ takeaways are coming when it counts. According to this X Post, Las Vegas has 10 takeaways in the fourth quarter of games. That leads the league by three. NFL defenses ranked by 4th quarter takeaways: pic.twitter.com/WPp6dQq4Hd — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 24, 2026 Las Vegas has compiled those 10 fourth-quarter takeaways in six of their 11 games. They got fourth-quarter takeaways in all four of their wins this season and two came in defeats. Of course, they had four against the New Orleans Saints in a Week 3 win. So, this is a heck of a formula for the Raiders to find a way to win. If they can get their opponents to cough up the ball late, Las Vegas has a real chance to win. Let’s see if they can force the Cleveland Browns into a late turnover on Sunday night.

item.title: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report
item.description: Real Madrid set to block exit of four players in January; two allowed to leave – report With the January transfer window just around the corner, Real Madrid are bracing themselves for relative peace and quiet, especially after a busy summer. The club are not expected to sign any new players in the winter transfer window. However, it is worth mentioning that a series of existing stars are facing an uncertain future and could leave in January. Endrick, Thiago Pitarch and Brahim Diaz are some of the many Real Madrid players facing an uncertain future at Santiago Bernabeu. Real Madrid, though, have a plan. Four exits to be blocked According to Miguel Serrano (h/t Defensa Central ), Real Madrid have made their mind up, as far as the club’s dealings in the January transfer window is concerned. The club are expected to block the exit of all the players who have been linked with a move away from Bernabeu this season, including Endrick. Brahim Diaz won’t be allowed to leave Real Madrid in January. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The exits of Trent Alexander-Arnold, Pitarch and Diaz are also expected to be blocked, as Jose Mourinho consider all of them key parts of the setup. It appears Mourinho is wary that any injury crisis during the second half of the campaign could make these players handy, as they offer plenty of quality to the table. Endrick, in particular, boasts immense talent and has been linked with a move away. But he has the backing of Mourinho . The same goes for Pitarch, even though the midfielder has barely played any football this season. Two exceptions to Real Madrid Serrano adds that Real Madrid have made an exception to this policy for two players in the form of Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio. Both these defenders are allowed to leave the club in the January transfer window, having failed to find themselves in Mourinho’s plans this season. Ferland Mendy is no longer needed at Real Madrid. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) Asencio, for one, has struggled with injuries and several off-field controversies. He has also looked like a shadow of his former self. His departure, therefore, could be a major positive for Real Madrid. Mendy, on the other hand, has a lucrative salary at Bernabeu despite having his entire career at Real Madrid marred by injuries . With Marc Cucurella and Alvaro Carreras, Real Madrid look quite stacked at left-back and no longer require the services of Mendy, whose contract expires in 2028. These are, however, still early days and if a lucrative market opportunity comes, Real Madrid will not shy away from making a few more exceptions.

item.description: FC Cincinnati stunned Major League Soccer experts with its 1-0 win over Nashville SC in the first game of their best-of-three playoff series at Nashville’s GEODIS park. They will now have two chances to move on to the Eastern Conference semifinals. The first is at home, 6:30 p.m. Nov. 28 at TQL Stadium. Game 3, if needed, will be 8 p.m. Dec. 2 back in Nashville. As the No. 9 seed in the Eastern Conference, this will be the last home game for Cincinnati in the conference playoffs. The only team in the Western Conference they could host in the MLS Cup final is Real Salt Lake, the No. 9 seed. The team is ready for what could be their last home game. “Trying to make sure that we step on the field with a really strong mindset,” said head coach Pat Noonan. “I know there's confidence, but there's also still a respect factor for how strong Nashville is, and we need to find ways to have our fan base lively, and a lot of times that comes with our play. It’s always nice to be having home games in the playoffs, and having that energy, that feel around the city, so hopefully we can take advantage of it.” Sure, Cincinnati’s winning goal came on a lucky break via a disastrous mistake by Nashville in the seventh minute of play, when Patrick Yazbek made a panicked back pass into his own net from 18 yards. But Cincinnati served notice with its defense the rest of the way, shutting out the best regular-season team in MLS history. Nashville had 22 shots, six on goal. item.description: An extended week of NFL coverage continues on Friday afternoon, with the league’s fourth annual Black Friday Football game. item.title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni celebrates wild Thanksgiving win in Cowboys fans’ faces
item.description: Sirianni celebrates Nick Sirianni gave Cowboys fans some salt for their Thanksgiving meals. The Eagles coach, moments after defeating their rivals on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left for a 39-38 victory , beelined for the field-level suites at AT&T Stadium in Dallas in a quick reminder of what just happened. Sirianni’s celebration was filled with some one-finger salutes from the Cowboys faithful and a short-lived one, as he was whisked away by Philadelphia’s chief security officer “Big Dom” DiSandro before things got too hairy. Nick Sirianni celebrated in front of the Cowboys fans after the Eagles comeback win ( FOX) pic.twitter.com/mR8isTM2Zh — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 27, 2026 Not that DiSandro didn’t get his licks in. The Herculean 34-year-old was caught trolling former Eagles defensive backs coach and current Cowboys defense coordinator Christian Parker, who recently had his play calling duties taken away by Dallas, before the game, teasing him with an Eagles hat. The win completed the largest-ever Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, with the Eagles trailing 31-10 in the third quarter. Quarterback Joe Milton, in just his third start for Philadelphia — and against his old team — threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, while adding a rushing score. “He played his butt off,” Sirianni said. “He played really good, made some throws that only he can make. He played an outstanding game, was super composed throughout, played the next play consistently.” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts after beating the Dallas Cowboys. AP Photo/Sam Hodde His heroics set the stage for veteran kicker Jake Elliott, who drilled a 59-yard field goal to give Philadelphia the miraculous win. “It’s awesome,” Elliott said. “Those are ones that I’ll remember for the rest of my life.” The Eagles, now 4-7, seemingly have life with two straight wins following seven consecutive losses. They remain in the NFC East basement, but beating the rival Cowboys (5-7) definitely provided some fire for Sirianni and his crew.

item.title: Iraola hails Isak's response as Liverpool striker hits top form
item.description: Alexander Isak has scored 10 goals for Liverpool this season (NICOLAS TUCAT) Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has praised Alexander Isak's response to his exacting tactical demands after the forward reached 10 goals for the club this season. The 27-year-old had a turbulent, injury-hit first campaign at Anfield but is now showing why Liverpool paid £125 million ($164 million) to prise him from Newcastle last year. In September, Iraola spoke about how his "fights" with the Sweden international were about the work he needed to do off the ball. Over the subsequent two months there has been a marked change in Isak's ability to fulfil Iraola's demands. In Wednesday's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge, Isak's pressing before his opener unsettled goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He also scored a second goal late in the game. "He has definitely improved a lot on the ball and without the ball," Iraola told reporters ahead of Sunday's Merseyside derby at Everton. "He is understanding better the press and the better he understands the press the less he has to run also. "Also on the ball we are using him much better in possession, he is linking up play very well. Technically he is a very nice player so I think we have to use him not just in the finishing side, he can be very important in our build-up." Iraola, in his first season at Anfield, praised Isak's performance during last week's 4-0 humbling of Manchester United, which lifted Liverpool to fourth in the table, as well as his display in Belgium. "I think he is understanding everything and is ready to learn and even improve more and it is a good sign," the Spaniard said on Friday. Former Bournemouth manager Iraola is looking forward to his first taste of a Merseyside derby. "I know I haven't lived this derby, but it doesn't take a lot when you are here to perceive that it's a big game for everyone involved," he said. "I'm very happy to be part of it and I hope I enjoy it, and to enjoy it there is only one way –- that is to win the game." item.description: The hole-in-one looked like a mistake the moment the ball left Robbie Minns’ club. The payoff? A brand-new BMW, worth about $160,000. Minns, a club professional at Camden Golf Club in southwest Sydney, stepped to the par-3 18th Friday during the second round of the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club and immediately took one hand off the club after impact. Turns out there was nothing wrong with the shot. The ball landed in the middle of the green, tracked toward the flag and disappeared into the cup, setting off a wild celebration from the group of friends following Minns around the course. The ace came with quite a bonus. Minns won a new BMW X5 valued at roughly $160,000 for making the hole-in-one. item.title: Tottenham dealt major blow as Roberto De Zerbi rules winger Savio out of the Christmas schedule with hamstring injury
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Crystal Palace FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Savio will miss Tottenham's festive fixtures and could be sidelined for up to 80 days with a hamstring injury. The Brazilian winger broke down less than half an hour after returning from the same problem in the 2-0 win over Ipswich, leaving Spurs without one of their most expensive summer signings during the busiest stretch of the season. De Zerbi delivers grim Savio update Savio came off the bench in the 64th minute of last Saturday's victory over Ipswich, but was forced off with two minutes left after a recurrence of the injury that had ruled him out of four league games. Asked at his press conference ahead of Sunday's trip to Sunderland whether the winger could miss the rest of the year, De Zerbi said: "Yeah, I think so. Unfortunately it's a tough situation to accept. He's a new guy and he's suffering with these new injuries. But this is football, if you see other European clubs they're all suffering these injuries." 'He will be crucial for us' The Ipswich win was Savio's first appearance in six weeks, according to BBC Sport , and there had already been fears that he faced weeks on the sidelines after he left the pitch visibly distraught. De Zerbi has now admitted he cannot put a date on his return. "Now he needs time. He needs hard work with the medical staff," the Italian added. "Then in 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don't know, when he comes back, he will be crucial for us in the last step of the season." Frustrating start to Spurs career The 22-year-old has endured a frustrating start to life in north London since his summer move from Manchester City in a deal that could reach £85 million. He has featured in only five of Tottenham's 11 Premier League games and is still waiting for his first league goal or assist. Savio did score and assist on his debut in a 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton in August. His absence adds to an injury list that already includes Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk, Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert, while Lucas Bergvall is a doubt with illness. Spurs face busy December Tottenham, who are 10th after four wins from their past five matches, visit 18th-placed Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. They then host Fulham on December 3 before welcoming champions Arsenal for the north London derby three days later.

item.title: NBC avoids Deshaun Watson in SNF promo
item.description: Credit: NBC The Cleveland Browns have been a great story so far in the 2026 season, a team once considered in the running for the first overall pick, now in playoff position with a 6-4 record. But Deshaun Watson will always be the elephant in the room for the franchise. Improbably, the Browns are being flexed into a late-November Sunday Night Football primetime game against the Raiders this week. It’s their first SNF game since 2021. Usually, any network would promote the biggest stars on the team to talk about the upcoming game. Nine times out of ten, that’s the quarterback. But Deshaun Watson isn’t exactly the most marketable person in the NFL. In fact, he may be the least, thanks to the 27 women who filed suit against him over sexual misconduct and his subsequent suspension from the league. So it shouldn’t be a surprise that on Thanksgiving night, with millions of families watching around the country, NBC decided to use second-year Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger alongside Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza on their game graphic. https://t.co/hcHJQlBRr7 — welovesports40 (@welovesports40) November 27, 2026 Interestingly, astute viewers noticed that Watson was used last week on SNF to promote the game. But NBC decided to go with Schwesinger for Thanksgiving. NBC took Deshaun Watson off their promotional graphic for the Browns-Raiders SNF game. Picture 1: Promotional graphic from Sunday night Picture 2: Promotional graphic tonight. https://t.co/l6qDvPpNSh — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 When was the last time that a second-year linebacker was used as a star player for a network promo for a primetime game? Schwesinger is a great player. He was the Defensive Rookie of the Year last year for a reason. But let’s be honest, only Browns fans or hardcore NFL fans are going to know who he is or what he looks like. It is peculiar that NBC felt comfortable enough with Deshaun Watson to put him on the graphic, only to remove him later. But perhaps the network had remorse or received pushback over featuring someone with such a controversial past. But as long as Watson is in the NFL and playing for the Browns, it’s always going to cause awkward, uncomfortable moments for everyone involved. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup.
